newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Iomega busy as stock whipsaws.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Iomega busy as stock whipsaws.

text.p: Options on shares of Iomega Corp were active and volatility increased Friday as the stock had a rollercoaster session.
At 1430 CDT/1930 GMT, Iomega shares were down 3/8 at 17-1/2 after climbing to 19-7/8. Turnover was more than 17 million shares. Thursday, the stock rallied three points.
"Evidently something's coming out. It looks like there's a lot of speculation going on there," said an options trader.
Both calls and puts on Iomega were active, suggesting investors were playing for both a further rise in the stock and a correction.
Analysts pegged the stock's early rise to news its internal Zip drives would be fully bootable.
Iomega options are traded on four of the five options exchanges, with the bulk of the activity on American Stock Exchange (AMEX) and Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE).
The Iomega September 20 calls were the most active, with a combined volume of more than 10,000. The option, which expires on Friday, had open interest of about 7,800.
The October 20 calls traded a total of more than 7,400 contracts.
On AMEX, the October 20 call was up 3/8 at 1-3/4 and on CBOE it was up 9/16 at 1-7/8. Its open interest was 3,570.
Trading in the option was spotty until Thursday.
Tuesday, for example, 60 contracts traded on CBOE. Thirteen traded Wednesday.
"Early in the day there were public buyers of the Oct 20s," a trader at the CBOE said. "Now sellers are coming in."
"The stock blew through two strikes yesterday so that renewed interest in the 20s," he added.
Other actives included the September 17-1/2 calls and the September 20 calls, both of which expire Friday. In the October series, the 15, 17-1/2 and 22-1/2 calls were active.
On the put side, the September 17-1/2 option was active, as were the October 12-1/2s, 15s, 17-1/2s and 20s.
Among longer-dated maturities, call buying, led by the November 30, which traded more than 1,200 contracts, was seen through to February 1997. Puts activity trickled off after the November 17-1/2s.
Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners, said volatilities had surged on the Iomega options.

"What's been interesting about this rise in volatility is that it's not taken place because of demand for puts or from demand for calls," Schwarz said. "It's taken place because thre's been demand for both."
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said the stock's rise likely fueled interest in the options.
"Iomega was up yesterday and was up another point today, so everybody is jumping on the options," he said.
--Gregory Crawford, derivatives desk 312-408-8750
